reason: The passage explicitly portrays Yahweh as the savior and deliverer of the Hebrew people. Samuel declares to Israel: 'Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I brought Israel up out of Egypt, and I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians and out of the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.' Rather than being antagonistic, Yahweh responds to the people's request for a king by anointing Saul and empowering him with the Holy Spirit ('The Spirit of the Lord will rush upon you'). The only criticism implicit in the text is that the people have rejected their God in favor of human kingship, but Yahweh nonetheless fulfills their request and validates His choice of Saul. Throughout the passage, Yahweh is depicted as protective, responsive, and empowering toward the Hebrew people.
